name: Amharic
variant: Standard Amharic (Ethiopia, Addis Ababa usage) in Ge'ez (fidel) script
script: Ge'ez (Ethiopic) script, the fidel: an abugida of about 33 base letters, each in seven vowel orders, plus -wa forms; left to right
basis: Grammar order of FSI Amharic Basic Course units 1-12 (sounds; the definite -u; pronouns, ነው and plurals; possessive endings, 'have' አለኝ, prepositions; perfective; infinitive and imperfective; negatives; time; imperative), with the topics of University of Florida AHM1130 Beginning Amharic (greetings, introductions, classroom, numbers, time and prices, likes, directions, restaurant)
src: FSI Amharic Basic Course (Foreign Service Institute), contents page hosted by multilingualbooks.com: the grammar note headings of units 1-20

University of Florida, AHM1130 Beginning Amharic syllabus (Fall 2020 and the Hagos section): weekly themes; textbooks Kebede Gessesse, Basic Amharic: A Teaching Manual (2012), Bezza Ayalew, Let's Speak Amharic (2005), Appleyard, Colloquial Amharic (optional)
ELIAS online Amharic course page (Let's Learn Amharic): lesson list, starting with a lesson on the Ge'ez alphabet; themes only
note: The FSI course is taught in transcription and has no script lessons, so the fidel stage (its order, the rows in the traditional ሀ ለ ሐ መ order, the letters that sound the same and the -wa forms) is common course practice, backed only by ELIAS starting with the alphabet. The grammar order follows FSI units 1-12 and stops there (relative clauses and causatives are beyond A1); demonstratives (FSI unit 14) are moved earlier. The topics and their order (greetings, introductions, classroom, numbers, time, prices, likes, directions, restaurant) follow UF AHM1130. Questions, family and the -ን object are placed by my own judgment. All Amharic forms in the titles are from my own knowledge. The fsi-language-courses.org Amharic page was opened but not used: its unit list does not match the FSI contents.
hardest: The fidel: about 33 letters in seven vowel orders (over 200 shapes), with several letters that sound the same
The ejective consonants ቀ, ጠ, ጨ, ጰ, ጸ, and doubled consonants that the script does not show
Verbs built with prefixes and suffixes that mark person and gender (እሄዳለሁ, ትሄዳለህ, ትሄጃለሽ)
Verb-final word order and 'you' that changes for man or woman (አንተ / አንቺ)

items: How the fidel works: a consonant in seven vowel orders (በ ቡ ቢ ባ ቤ ብ ቦ)
Fidel rows ሀ to ቸ: ሀ ለ ሐ መ ሠ ረ ሰ ሸ ቀ በ ቨ ተ ቸ
Fidel rows ኀ to ዠ: ኀ ነ ኘ አ ከ ኸ ወ ዐ ዘ ዠ
Fidel rows የ to ፐ, with the ejectives ጠ ጨ ጰ ጸ: የ ደ ጀ ገ ጠ ጨ ጰ ጸ ፀ ፈ ፐ
Letters that sound the same (ሀ ሐ ኀ ኸ, ሰ ሠ, አ ዐ, ጸ ፀ), -wa forms (ቧ ሏ ኳ ጓ) and reading words
Greetings: ሰላም, ጤና ይስጥልኝ, እንደምን አደርክ? / አደርሽ?, አመሰግናለሁ
Introducing yourself: ስሜ … ነው, ስምህ ማን ነው? / ስምሽ ማን ነው?
Pronouns and 'to be': እኔ, አንተ, አንቺ, እሱ, እሷ with ነኝ, ነህ, ነሽ, ነው, ናት
This and that, and the classroom: ይህ, ይህች, ያ; መጽሐፍ, ብዕር
Question words: ምን, ማን, የት, መቼ, ስንት, እንዴት
Numbers: አንድ, ሁለት … አስር, ሃያ, መቶ
Possessive endings: ቤቴ, ቤትህ, ቤትሽ, ቤቱ, ቤቷ
Prepositions: በ-, ከ-, ለ-, ወደ (ከአሜሪካ ነኝ)
Past tense (perfective): ሄድኩ, ሄድክ, ሄደ, ሄደች; the object ending -ን (ቡናውን ጠጣሁ)
Present and future (imperfective): እሄዳለሁ, ትሄዳለህ, ይሄዳል
The infinitive and wanting: መሄድ, ቡና እፈልጋለሁ
Commands and please: ና, ነይ, ኑ, ተቀመጥ; እባክህ / እባክሽ
Ethiopian time and days: ስንት ሰዓት ነው?, the day counted from 6 a.m., ሰኞ, ማክሰኞ
Prices at the market: ዋጋው ስንት ነው?, ብር
At a restaurant: እንጀራ, ቡና, ውሃ, ሂሳብ
Directions: ወደ ቀኝ, ወደ ግራ, ቀጥታ; ሆቴሉ የት ነው?
